verdicts.summary: The snapshot of which tasks to clear is taken at line 1066, while the dying session's subscribers are still live. A roster update already sitting in a subscriber queue, but not yet saved, can land after the snapshot. That task's id is not in the snapshot, so the cleanup never removes it and the thread stays Waiting.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A Claude turn is running and the CLI reports a new background shell. The provider-thread event is offered to the run subscriber queue (publishToSubscribers, ProviderSessionManager.ts:2073) but not yet saved. 2) The thread is settled or archived, so detach calls releaseEntry (2528). 3) readReleasedBackgroundTasks (1066) reads the stored roster without the new task. 4) failSubscribers (1081) puts the failure signal behind the queued event (586-588), so a consumer that drains in order still saves the roster with the new task. 5) writeReleasedBackgroundWorkEvents re-reads, but it only removes ids from the snapshot (851), so the new task stays.
verdicts.missing: I did not read the consumer of the subscriber queues (the run event ingestion). I can't tell whether it saves events queued before the failure signal or drops them on failure or interrupt. Step 4 depends on that.

verdicts.summary: The only hazard in this compare-and-set is that it needs decode→encode of the stored row to give back the same bytes, which is finding 0. I also tried a missing row: the cleanup re-reads, finds no provider thread and returns (diff line 516). And the guard SELECT runs inside the same transaction as the write (commitThenPublish, EventSink.ts:257-279), the same as the sibling writers.

Single-thread (exclusive) sessions can never hold a thread that detached earlier without the session being released. Opening a session for a second thread is refused, and a detach that leaves no attached thread releases the session right away, passing that thread as detachedThreadId.
verdicts.scenario: Thread A detaches from a Claude or Muse session and the session stays live; a later idle release then misses A's roster. This is impossible: for a single-thread session, the detach that empties attachedThreadIds calls releaseEntry with detachedThreadId (2524-2533), and opening for a different thread is rejected (2176-2181). Claude (ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:270) and Muse (adapter.ts:99) both declare supportsMultipleProviderThreadsPerSession: false.
